item.name: Monsters Unleashed
item.description: Monsters rise across the Earth, and the Marvel Universe is suddenly under siege by creatures too massive and too strange for any one hero to stop. As the Avengers, X-Men, Guardians of the Galaxy, Inhumans, and Champions battle kaiju-sized nightmares around the world, a young boy named Kei Kawade may hold the key to the invasion—and to the monsters themselves. From Cullen Bunn, Steve McNiven, Greg Land, Salvador Larroca, Adam Kubert, and more, Monsters Unleashed turns Marvel’s greatest heroes into the last line of defense against an army of impossible beasts.

item.name: Secret Empire
item.description:
When a cosmic manipulation rewrites history, Captain America emerges as a loyal agent of Hydra—and uses his authority to dismantle the world from within. As Hydra seizes control of the United States, heroes are scattered, imprisoned, or forced underground, leaving a fractured resistance to fight back against a regime built on fear and control.

As the truth behind reality itself comes into question, the battle becomes more than a rebellion—it’s a fight to restore the very ideals Captain America once stood for.

Led by Nick Spencer and Steve McNiven, Secret Empire is a bold, controversial crossover—where the symbol of freedom becomes the face of tyranny.

item.name: Superman Reborn
item.description:
Superman’s past and present collide when reality itself begins to unravel around him. With his family at the center of a growing distortion, Clark Kent, Lois Lane, and Jon Kent find themselves caught in a mystery that reaches back through fractured timelines and forgotten histories. As truths long buried come to light, the existence of two Supermen—and two versions of their lives—can no longer hold.

Facing a threat that twists identity and memory, Superman must confront who he has been and who he is meant to be. Superman: Reborn (2017) resolves the divide left behind by Flashpoint, merging two legacies into one and restoring a unified Man of Steel for the Rebirth era—stronger, whole, and finally complete.

item.name: The Doomsday Clock
item.description:
The truth behind a broken universe comes to light when two worlds collide. As the mystery seeded in Rebirth unfolds, Dr. Manhattan emerges from the shadows, revealing his hand in reshaping time itself—and altering the history of the DC Universe. With reality shifting and timelines rewriting around them, heroes and villains alike search for answers in a world that no longer fits together.

At the center stands Superman, the one figure even Manhattan cannot fully understand. As their paths converge, the fate of every timeline—and every version of the DC Universe—hangs in the balance. Written by Geoff Johns with precise, layered storytelling, Doomsday Clock (2017–2019) bridges worlds, restores legacy, and delivers a defining statement about why Superman remains the heart of everything.

item.name: Drowned Earth
item.description:
The seas rise—and they don’t come alone. When ancient ocean gods awaken to reclaim the planet, the world is swallowed beneath a relentless tide, turning cities into ruins and the surface into a drowned wasteland.

As the Justice League fights to survive a world sinking beneath them, Aquaman and Mera lead a desperate stand against forces older than humanity itself. But in a war where the ocean itself is the enemy, even the greatest heroes may not be enough to keep the world from drowning.

Led by Scott Snyder, James Tynion IV, and Joshua Williamson, Drowned Earth unleashes a global catastrophe from the depths—where survival means facing a world already lost to the tide.

item.name: Heroes in Crisis
item.description:
At Sanctuary, a secret refuge built by Batman, Superman, and Wonder Woman, heroes confront the trauma no battle can erase. But when the safe haven becomes the site of a brutal massacre, the DC Universe is forced to face a devastating truth—sometimes the greatest danger comes from within.

As the investigation unfolds, all eyes turn to Wally West, and the line between victim, hero, and culprit begins to blur.

Led by Tom King and Clay Mann, Heroes in Crisis is a deeply personal reckoning—where the cost of heroism can no longer be hidden, and the truth threatens to break what’s left of trust.

item.name: Infinity Countdown
item.description:
The Infinity Stones resurface—scattered across the Marvel Universe and claimed by unexpected hands, from heroes to cosmic outlaws. As a desperate race begins to secure them, each Stone brings its own danger, drawing the Guardians of the Galaxy and a host of others into a widening conflict.

But as the pieces fall into place, a far greater threat emerges: a twisted fusion of Ultron and Adam Warlock, whose plan could reshape existence itself. With the fate of the Stones—and reality—at stake, the countdown to catastrophe has already begun.

Led by Gerry Duggan and Mike Deodato Jr., Infinity Countdown is a cosmic prelude—where the hunt for ultimate power sets the stage for a universe-altering war.

item.name: Infinity Wars
item.description:
After seizing the Infinity Stones, Gamora—reborn as Requiem—uses their power to rewrite reality, folding the universe in half and merging heroes and villains into warped new identities.

As the fractured world gives rise to impossible hybrids like Arachknight and Soldier Supreme, a small group of survivors uncovers the truth: reality itself has been reshaped from within the Soul World. To restore what was lost, they must confront a universe where nothing is what it should be—and where every victory comes at the cost of another life erased.

Led by Gerry Duggan and Mike Deodato Jr., Infinity Wars is a reality-bending crossover—where identity, power, and sacrifice collide in a universe remade.

item.name: Milk Wars
item.description:
When the Retconn Corporation rewrites reality into a sterile, all-American dream, the Justice League becomes a lineup of smiling, obedient parodies—led by the eerie Milkman Man.

Only the Doom Patrol—DC’s strangest heroes—can fight back, breaking the rules of the universe itself to restore everything that makes it messy, human, and real.

Led by Gerard Way and Steve Orlando, Milk Wars is a surreal collision between corporate perfection and chaotic creativity—where saving the world means refusing to let it become too perfect to matter.

Cave Carson Has a Cybernetic Eye/Swamp Thing Special

item.name: No Justice
item.description:
In the wake of cosmic upheaval, the universe fractures under threats too vast for any one team to face. Even villains must become allies as Brainiac forces the heroes of Earth into uneasy alliances, dividing them into new Justice League teams built to confront the rising power of ancient Omega Titans.

As the boundaries of reality strain and the Source itself hangs in the balance, icons like Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman must redefine what justice means in a universe where survival demands cooperation with their greatest enemies.

Led by Scott Snyder, James Tynion IV, and Joshua Williamson, No Justice reshapes the Justice League into something new—launching a cosmic era where the fate of existence itself rests on uneasy unity.

item.name: Spider-Geddon
item.description:
The Inheritors return, escaping their prison and reigniting the hunt across the Spider-Verse. With the original Spider-Army fractured and Peter Parker absent from the center of the fight, a new generation of Spider-heroes must rally across realities before the Inheritors devour every Spider-totem in existence.

As Miles Morales, Spider-Gwen, Superior Spider-Man, Spider-Woman, and countless alternate web-slingers join the war, the battle becomes more than survival—it is a test of whether the Spider-Verse can stand without its most familiar Spider-Man leading it.

Led by Christos Gage, Dan Slott, Jorge Molina, Carlo Barberi, and other creators, Spider-Geddon is the explosive sequel to Spider-Verse—a multiversal Spider-crossover where every web connects to a fight for existence.

item.name: The Witching Hour
item.description:
When the source of all magic turns hostile, the ancient goddess Hecate rises to reclaim the power she seeded across the world. Marked as her unwilling vessel, Wonder Woman becomes the center of a growing magical storm that threatens to erase sorcery itself.

As reality warps and spells spiral out of control, the Justice League Dark must confront the origin of magic—and decide whether saving the world means ending magic forever.

Led by James Tynion IV, The Witching Hour is a dark turning point where myth, magic, and destiny collide—and nothing supernatural emerges unchanged.

item.name: Absolute Carnage
item.description:
Cletus Kasady returns as something worse than a serial killer—reborn through the cult of Knull and driven to awaken the god of the symbiotes. To do it, Carnage begins hunting everyone who has ever bonded with a symbiote, tearing through heroes, villains, and civilians alike in a blood-soaked campaign to gather the codices hidden in their spines.

As Venom, Spider-Man, and their allies fight to protect Carnage’s targets, the threat grows from street-level horror into cosmic prophecy. Every victim brings Knull closer, and every battle reveals that Carnage is not the final nightmare—he is only the herald.

Led by Donny Cates and Ryan Stegman, Absolute Carnage is a brutal symbiote crossover where body horror, legacy, and cosmic darkness collide—setting the stage for King in Black.

issues.series_name: Web of Venom: The Good Son

item.name: City of Bane
item.description: In City of Bane, writer Tom King and artists Mikel Janín and Tony S. Daniel bring Batman’s long war to a breaking point as Bane finally conquers Gotham, turning it into a controlled, silent dictatorship. With Batman defeated and driven out, the city falls under the rule of Bane and an unexpected ally—Thomas Wayne—who believes destroying Bruce is the only way to save him. As Bruce fights his way back alongside Catwoman, the story builds to a final confrontation that tests not just his strength, but what Batman truly stands for.

item.name: Event Leviathan
item.description:
The world’s intelligence networks collapse overnight. A.R.G.U.S., Spyral, Checkmate—gone. In their place rises Leviathan, a shadow organization with a single goal: reshape the world by tearing down the systems that controlled it.

As secrets burn and trust evaporates, Superman, Lois Lane, and The Question lead a desperate investigation, where every ally is a suspect and every answer only deepens the mystery.

Led by Brian Michael Bendis and Alex Maleev, Event Leviathan is a slow-burn conspiracy thriller—where the greatest threat to the DC Universe isn’t power, but control.

issues.series_name: DC's Year of the Villain Special

item.name: House of X / Powers of X
item.description: The dream has changed. On the living island of Krakoa, Charles Xavier offers mutantkind a future unlike anything humanity imagined—and the world must reckon with his terms. But behind this bold new beginning lies a secret that reshapes everything. Across two interwoven series spanning generations, Jonathan Hickman launches a revolutionary era for the X-Men. Twelve issues. One vision. Everything changes.

item.name: The Terminus Agenda
item.description:
When past sins resurface, a ruthless plan pulls Batman and Deathstroke into open conflict over the fate of Damian Wayne. As the Teen Titans are drawn into the crossfire, loyalties fracture and the line between mentorship and manipulation begins to blur.

With control of Robin’s future at stake, the battle becomes more than a clash of enemies—it’s a war over legacy, identity, and the kind of hero Damian will become.

Led by Joshua Williamson, Adam Glass, and Tom King, The Terminus Agenda is a tense crossover where the cost of shaping a hero may be losing him entirely.

item.name: War of the Realms
item.description:
After conquering the Ten Realms, Malekith brings the final war to Earth—unleashing an invasion of dark elves, frost giants, and monsters that turns the world into a battlefield.

As the Avengers rally alongside heroes from across realms and mythologies, Thor and his allies must lead a desperate stand to stop a war that has already consumed the cosmos. With realms falling and hope fading, victory will demand sacrifice—and the rise of new legends to carry the fight forward.

Led by Jason Aaron and Russell Dauterman, War of the Realms is a sweeping mythic crossover—where gods, monsters, and heroes collide in a final battle for every realm.

item.name: Year of the Villain
item.description:
In the aftermath of cosmic upheaval, the balance of power shifts—and the villains strike first. Transformed into something more than human, Lex Luthor unites the Legion of Doom and offers power to villains across the world, turning ambition into domination and chaos into strategy.

As heroes struggle to respond to a world tilting out of their control, the influence of the Batman Who Laughs spreads in the shadows, warping allies and enemies alike and pushing reality toward something far darker.

Spanning the entire DC Universe, Year of the Villain marks the moment evil stops reacting—and starts winning.

item.name: Dark Nights: Death Metal
item.description: In Dark Nights: Death Metal, writer Scott Snyder and artist Greg Capullo unleash a full-throttle finale to their DC saga as the Batman Who Laughs ascends to godlike power and reshapes reality into a nightmarish wasteland. With the Justice League scattered and hope nearly extinguished, it falls to Wonder Woman to rise beyond everything she’s been before and lead one last stand against the end of all things. Blending heavy metal spectacle with cosmic stakes, Death Metal is a loud, chaotic, and ultimately hopeful celebration of the DC Universe at its most mythic.

item.name: Empyre
item.description:
A fragile peace between the Kree and Skrull empires—united under Hulkling—is shattered when the plant-based Cotati launch a surprise assault on Earth, seeking to wipe out all animal life. As the Avengers and the Fantastic Four rally to defend the planet, a cosmic war erupts that blurs the line between ally and enemy.

With ancient rivalries set aside and new alliances tested, the battle spans Earth and the stars, forcing heroes to confront a threat rooted in survival itself.

Led by Al Ewing, Dan Slott, and Valerio Schiti, Empyre is a cosmic crossover—where unity is tested against extinction, and the fate of two empires hangs in the balance.

item.name: Endless Winter
item.description: In Endless Winter, writers Andy Lanning and Ron Marz, alongside a rotating team of artists, plunge the DC Universe into a sudden ice age as the ancient Frost King rises to finish a war that began in the age of Black Adam. As the Justice League struggles to survive a frozen world, the story weaves past and present together, revealing a forgotten chapter of heroism and sacrifice. Blending mythic history with high-stakes action, Endless Winter delivers a fast-moving crossover where legacy and ancient power collide.

item.name: The Joker War
item.description: In Joker War, writer James Tynion IV and artist Jorge Jiménez unleash a full-scale assault on Gotham as the Joker seizes Bruce Wayne’s fortune and turns it into a weapon of chaos. With Batman stripped of his resources and the city pushed to the brink, allies like Harley Quinn and the Bat-family are forced into a desperate fight to reclaim Gotham. Introducing the deadly new wildcard Punchline, the story delivers a relentless clash that leaves Batman changed—no longer defined by wealth, but by what remains when everything is taken away.

item.name: X of Swords
item.description: When the ancient enemy of Arakko breaks through the gates of Otherworld, Krakoa’s champions must take up legendary blades and face a tournament where victory may cost more than death. From Jonathan Hickman, Tini Howard, Pepe Larraz, Leinil Francis Yu, Mahmud Asrar, and more, X of Swords transforms the Dawn of X into a mythic mutant epic of prophecy, betrayal, magic, and survival.

item.name: Devil's Reign
item.description:
As mayor of New York, Kingpin outlaws superheroes and unleashes a citywide crackdown, deploying his own Thunderbolts to hunt anyone who resists. With the truth about his past erased and power firmly in his hands, Fisk turns the system itself into a weapon.

As heroes are imprisoned or forced underground, Daredevil, Elektra, and their allies lead a resistance against a regime built on control, corruption, and fear. But with the Purple Man pulling strings behind the scenes, the battle for the city becomes a fight for free will itself.

Led by Chip Zdarsky and Marco Checchetto, Devil’s Reign is a grounded crossover—where power isn’t cosmic, but political, and the war for New York is fought in the shadows.

item.name: Fear State
item.description: In Fear State, writer James Tynion IV and artist Jorge Jiménez push Gotham to the brink as Scarecrow unleashes a calculated campaign of terror designed to plunge the city into controlled chaos. With the Magistrate tightening its grip and Batman stretched to his limits, allies like Oracle and the Bat-family fight to prevent Gotham from becoming a fully realized police state. Blending psychological warfare with near-future dystopia, Fear State brings the post–Joker War era to a head as Gotham’s future—and Batman’s role within it—hang in the balance.

item.name: Generations
item.description: In Generations, writer Dan Jurgens and a lineup of artists weave a time-spanning adventure that stitches together the entire history of the DC Universe. When a mysterious threat begins unraveling reality, heroes from different eras—including Batman, Superman, and Booster Gold—are pulled across time to preserve the legacy of their world. Moving from the Golden Age to the far future, the story celebrates DC’s past while redefining how its timeline fits together, offering a sweeping, connective look at the heroes who shaped it.

item.name: Heroes Reborn
item.description:
In a world where the Avengers never existed, Earth’s mightiest heroes are replaced by the Squadron Supreme—led by Hyperion—who stand as the planet’s unquestioned protectors.

But as reality begins to fracture, Blade is the only one who remembers the truth: this world is a lie. As he searches for answers, a hidden war between cosmic forces—tied to the Phoenix Force and Mephisto—threatens to unravel everything.

Led by Jason Aaron and Ed McGuinness, Heroes Reborn is a reality-twisting crossover—where the absence of the Avengers reveals just how much the world depends on them.

item.name: Infinite Frontier
item.description: In Infinite Frontier, writer Joshua Williamson and artist Xermanico chart a new course for the DC Universe in the wake of Dark Nights: Death Metal, where every era now exists within an expanded Multiverse. As Barry Allen explores the reborn frontier of infinite worlds, a darker threat emerges in the shadows—Darkseid, evolving into something far more dangerous than before. Blending cosmic mystery with a redefined sense of legacy, Infinite Frontier lays the foundation for a universe where nothing is lost and everything matters.

item.name: King in Black
item.description:
The god of the symbiotes, Knull, descends on Earth with a living darkness—unleashing a global symbiote invasion that overwhelms heroes and consumes the sky itself. As cities fall and even cosmic beings are corrupted, the Marvel Universe is plunged into a night without hope.

With the Avengers and their allies pushed to the brink, the fight centers on Venom, whose connection to the symbiotes may be the key to stopping the god who created them. In a war against a force older than the universe, victory will require more than strength—it will demand becoming something greater.

Led by Donny Cates and Ryan Stegman, King in Black is a dark cosmic crossover—where the universe itself is swallowed by shadow, and only one hero can rise to challenge a god.

item.name: Dark Crisis on Infinite Earths
item.description: In Dark Crisis on Infinite Earths, writer Joshua Williamson and artist Daniel Sampere usher in a new generation of heroes after the apparent fall of the Justice League. As worlds begin to collapse under the influence of Pariah and a growing multiversal threat, figures like Nightwing and Jon Kent step forward to lead a fractured resistance. Blending legacy, loss, and cosmic stakes, the story reaffirms the enduring spirit of heroism while redefining who stands at the center of the DC Universe.

item.name: Dark Web
item.description:
Old resentments crawl back into the light when Ben Reilly and Madelyne Pryor join forces, turning their shared history of rejection into a supernatural assault on New York. As demons flood the city and stolen memories twist into weapons, Spider-Man and the X-Men are dragged into a nightmare built from clones, betrayal, and unfinished pain.

With Limbo unleashed and the past refusing to stay buried, Peter Parker, Jean Grey, and their allies must face enemies who do not just want revenge—they want the lives and identities they believe were stolen from them.

Led by Zeb Wells, Adam Kubert, Al Ewing, Gerry Duggan, Rod Reis, and other creators, Dark Web is a Spider-Man/X-Men crossover where demonic chaos and clone trauma collide in one very weird war for identity.

item.name: Flashpoint Beyond
item.description: In Flashpoint Beyond, writer Geoff Johns alongside Jeremy Adams and Tim Sheridan, with art by Xermanico, return to the fractured world of Flashpoint as Thomas Wayne searches for answers in a timeline that shouldn’t exist. As reality begins to shift and hidden forces manipulate time itself, Thomas is drawn into a mystery tied to his past, his family, and the lingering consequences of the original Flashpoint. Blending noir detective work with multiversal intrigue, Flashpoint Beyond expands the legacy of a broken world that refuses to stay buried.

item.name: Judgment Day
item.description:
War erupts between the Eternals and the X-Men when the Eternals declare mutants to be deviants—forcing the Avengers into a conflict that threatens to consume the planet. But as the fighting escalates, a greater power awakens: a reborn Celestial that judges all of Earth in real time.

As humanity—and every hero—faces individual judgment, the battle shifts from survival to worthiness. In a world where every secret is exposed and every soul weighed, saving Earth may depend not on strength, but on proving it deserves to survive.

Led by Kieron Gillen and Valerio Schiti, Judgment Day is a sweeping crossover—where war, morality, and cosmic judgment collide, and the fate of the world is decided one verdict at a time.

issues.phase: Prelude: The War Before the War

item.name: Shadow War
item.description: In Shadow War, writer Joshua Williamson and artists Viktor Bogdanović and Howard Porter ignite a deadly conflict after the apparent assassination of Ra's al Ghul, setting Deathstroke against the Batman family in a globe-spanning clash of assassins. As Talia al Ghul seeks vengeance and Damian Wayne is pulled between loyalty and legacy, the truth behind the killing threatens to ignite something far worse. Blending espionage, family tension, and high-stakes action, Shadow War pushes its characters to the edge as alliances fracture and secrets come to light.

item.name: The New Golden Age
item.description: In The New Golden Age, writer Geoff Johns and artist Jerry Ordway open a new chapter in DC’s legacy as time itself begins to fracture, scattering heroes and secrets across decades. At the center is Stargirl, whose discovery of hidden histories and lost sidekicks reveals a forgotten generation of heroes tied to the Justice Society of America. Blending mystery, time travel, and Golden Age legacy, the story reshapes DC’s past to expand its future, setting the stage for a new era of heroes rising from history itself.

item.name: Trial of the Amazons
item.description: In Trial of the Amazons, writers Becky Cloonan, Michael W. Conrad, and Joëlle Jones unite the three Amazon tribes—themyscirans, Bana-Mighdall, and the Esquecida—in a fragile gathering that erupts into war after a shocking murder. With Wonder Woman absent, leaders like Hippolyta and Nubia struggle to prevent all-out conflict as secrets and old rivalries surface. Blending political intrigue with mythic action, the story reshapes Amazon unity and legacy while setting a new path forward for their world.

Trial of the Amazons: Wonder Girl

item.name: War for Earth-3
item.description: In War for Earth-3, writer Robbie Thompson and artist Dexter Soy collide the Suicide Squad with the twisted world of Earth-3, where the Crime Syndicate rules without opposition. As Amanda Waller pushes her agenda across dimensions, a brutal conflict erupts between two ruthless forces, blurring the line between heroes and villains. Expanding the fallout of Infinite Frontier, the story dives into a world where power reigns unchecked and survival means choosing the lesser evil.

item.name: Fall of X/Rise of the Powers of X
item.description:
Krakoa falls. After years of mutant power, resurrection, and fragile nationhood, the enemies of mutantkind strike at the heart of the dream, scattering the X-Men and turning survival into resistance once again.

As Orchis tightens its grip and mutantkind faces extinction on multiple fronts, the conflict expands beyond Earth, beyond politics, and into the architecture of time itself. Across collapsing futures and desperate last stands, the X-Men fight not only to save Krakoa, but to decide whether the dream can survive in any form at all.

Led by Gerry Duggan, Kieron Gillen, Al Ewing, Jonathan Hickman, R.B. Silva, Lucas Werneck, Stefano Caselli, and other creators, Fall of X / Rise of the Powers of X is the endgame of the Krakoa era—where paradise collapses, futures burn, and mutantkind makes one final stand for the world it tried to build.

item.name: Gotham War
item.description: In Gotham War, writers Chip Zdarsky and Tini Howard, with art by Jorge Jiménez and Nico Leon, fracture Gotham along ideological lines as Batman and Catwoman clash over how to save their city. While Catwoman trains criminals to operate under a controlled system that avoids violence, Batman sees only a dangerous escalation, pushing the Bat-family into opposing sides of a growing conflict. Blending moral tension with street-level stakes, Gotham War turns allies into adversaries as Gotham becomes the battleground for two visions of justice.

item.name: Knight Terrors
item.description: In Knight Terrors, writer Joshua Williamson and artist Howard Porter plunge the DC Universe into a waking nightmare as the villain Insomnia traps the world in a dreamlike horror realm. With heroes like Batman and the Justice League lost within their darkest fears, it falls to Deadman to navigate the nightmare and rally what remains of Earth’s defenders. Blending supernatural horror with psychological stakes, Knight Terrors explores the fears that haunt even the greatest heroes—and what it takes to wake up from them.

item.name: Lazarus Planet
item.description: In Lazarus Planet, writer Mark Waid and artist Riccardo Federici unleash a global magical catastrophe when the eruption of a Lazarus Volcano floods the world with unpredictable energy, transforming powers, twisting reality, and unleashing ancient forces. As Batman and Robin struggle to contain the chaos, heroes and villains alike are reshaped by a world where magic now overrides the natural order. Blending spectacle with mythic stakes, Lazarus Planet reshapes the role of magic in the DC Universe and sets the stage for what comes next.

item.name: One-Minute War
item.description: In One-Minute War, writer Jeremy Adams and artists Roger Cruz and Fernando Pasarin push the Flash Family into a high-speed war against the alien Fraction, a race that can move as fast as they do. With time effectively frozen for the rest of the world, Wally West and his allies must fight an entire invasion in the span of a single minute. Blending relentless action with family-driven stakes, One-Minute War turns the Speed Force into a battlefield where only the fastest—and the most united—can survive.

item.name: Sins of Sinister
item.description:
When Mister Sinister finally corrupts the heart of Krakoa’s resurrection system, the mutant dream becomes a nightmare that spreads across time. What begins as a quiet genetic victory turns into a thousand-year dystopia, as Sinisterized mutants reshape Earth, the galaxy, and eventually reality itself in their own twisted image.

Across shifting futures of war, empire, betrayal, and cosmic horror, the X-Men’s greatest achievement becomes their greatest vulnerability. To save mutantkind, the survivors must unravel a timeline where Sinister has already won—and where every resurrection only deepens the infection.

Led by Kieron Gillen, Al Ewing, Si Spurrier, Lucas Werneck, Paco Medina, and other creators, Sins of Sinister is a high-concept Krakoa-era crossover—where immortality becomes corruption, and the future mutates into something monstrous.

item.name: Absolute Power
item.description: In Absolute Power, writer Mark Waid and artist Dan Mora unleash a sweeping DC event as Amanda Waller executes a long-planned takeover, stripping heroes of their powers and turning Earth’s defenses against them. With icons like Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman suddenly vulnerable, a fractured resistance must rise against a world where the balance of power has been completely inverted. Blending espionage, large-scale conflict, and a unifying threat, Absolute Power pushes the DC Universe into a fight for survival without its greatest advantage.

issues.series_name: Free Comic Book Day 2024: Absolute Power Special Edition

item.name: Beast War
item.description: In Titans: Beast World, writer Tom Taylor and artist Ivan Reis unleash a global crisis when Beast Boy taps into a dangerous new level of power, transforming himself—and eventually much of the world—into unpredictable animal forms. As the Titans step into the spotlight as Earth’s primary defenders, a spreading infection tied to alien forces threatens to turn humanity into something wild and uncontrollable. Blending spectacle with character-driven stakes, Beast World tests the Titans’ leadership in a world where survival means embracing chaos.

item.name: Blood Hunt
item.description:
The sun goes out—and the night takes over. As a coordinated vampire uprising blankets the world in darkness, the Avengers and their allies are thrust into a global war against an enemy that has been preparing for centuries.

With cities falling and heroes overwhelmed, figures like Blade, Doctor Strange, and Moon Knight must navigate a world where every shadow hides a threat—and survival means fighting an enemy that thrives in the dark.

Led by Jed MacKay and Pepe Larraz, Blood Hunt is a supernatural crossover—where the Marvel Universe is plunged into eternal night, and the hunt has only just begun.

item.name: DC K.O.
item.description:
Darkseid has returned as something greater than a god: King Omega, a cosmic force powerful enough to destroy the future and remake Earth in the image of Apokolips. With time running out, the heroes of the DC Universe enter a brutal tournament where victory is not about glory—it is about gathering enough power to challenge the end itself. DC described the event as a cosmic tournament to save the universe from Darkseid, with Scott Snyder framing it as a “knock-down, drag-out fight” among DC’s heroes.

As Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, the Justice League, Titans, and heroes across the DCU are pulled into the fight, every battle becomes a test of strength, sacrifice, and identity. To stop Darkseid before he transforms the world into his final kingdom, the champions of Earth must survive each other first.

Led by Scott Snyder, Joshua Williamson, Javier Fernández, and Xermánico, DC K.O. is a high-energy Crisis-scale slugfest—where the road to salvation runs through the arena, and the only way to save the universe is to win the fight of your life.

item.description: Brian Azzarello and Cliff Chiang's New 52 run reimagined Wonder Woman as a dark mythological horror-adventure, recasting the Olympian gods as dangerous, scheming figures and Diana as their reluctant champion. One of the most acclaimed DC New 52 titles.

item.title: Wonder Woman by George Pérez
item.description: George Pérez's landmark relaunch of Wonder Woman post-Crisis, reimagining Diana's origin with deep roots in Greek mythology and feminist themes. Widely considered the definitive modern foundation of the character.

categories.adaptation_notes: Wonder Woman (animated film, 2009)

item.title: Wonder Woman by Phil Jimenez
item.description: Phil Jimenez's celebrated run as writer-artist, deeply influenced by the Pérez era, featuring rich mythological storytelling, a landmark crossover with The Amazons Attack, and some of the most detailed and beautiful artwork in the title's history.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Amazonia
item.description: William Messner-Loebs and Phil Winslade's Elseworlds tale set in a Victorian-era alternate history where Diana is brought to a brutally patriarchal England. A dark, feminist fable that stands as one of the most distinctive Wonder Woman stories ever published.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Bitter Rivals
item.description: Greg Rucka's arc exploring the political and personal rivalry between Diana and Veronica Cale, establishing one of the most compelling antagonists in Wonder Woman's modern history.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Contagion
item.description: Gail Simone's arc in which a plague strikes the Amazons and Diana must navigate treachery from within while facing the villainous Genocide — a creature literally made from the soil of historical atrocities. One of the darkest and most ambitious chapters of Simone's run.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Dead Earth
item.description: Daniel Warren Johnson's post-apocalyptic reimagining finds Diana awakening in a ravaged future Earth, battling kaiju-scale monsters and confronting the legacy of heroism. A visceral, emotionally resonant limited series that became an instant fan favourite.

categories.adaptation_notes: Eisner Award — Best Limited Series (2021); Eisner Award — Best Writer/Artist (Daniel Warren Johnson, 2021)

item.title: Wonder Woman: Destiny Calling
item.description: Dan Mishkin and Gene Colan's run on the original series, including the landmark 300th issue celebration, representing a key transitional era for the character in the early 1980s before the Crisis reboot.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Down to Earth
item.description: Greg Rucka's opening arc on Wonder Woman, in which Diana publishes a book advocating Amazonian philosophy and faces political and media backlash. A sophisticated, character-driven examination of Diana as ambassador and public figure.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Ends of the Earth
item.description: Gail Simone pits Diana against Stalker and a demonic threat in a mythic quest narrative that showcases Diana's compassion and warrior spirit in equal measure.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Eyes of the Gorgon
item.description: Greg Rucka's continuation sees Diana face Medusa in a brutal, mythologically rich confrontation with devastating personal consequences. One of the most celebrated arcs of Rucka's acclaimed run.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Gods and Mortals
item.description: George Pérez's landmark relaunch of Wonder Woman post-Crisis, reimagining Diana's origin with deep roots in Greek mythology and feminist themes. Established the definitive modern template for the character.

categories.adaptation_notes: Wonder Woman (animated film, 2009) · Inspired Wonder Woman (film, 2017)

item.title: Wonder Woman: Historia: The Amazons
item.description: Kelly Sue DeConnick and Phil Jimenez's visually spectacular limited series recounts the mythic origin of the Amazons from the perspective of the goddesses themselves. Jimenez's artwork, rendered in an epic painted style, is widely considered some of the finest in DC's history.

categories.adaptation_notes: Eisner, Best Single Issue/One-Shot (2022) · Eisner, Best Penciller/Inker — Phil Jimenez (2022)

item.title: Wonder Woman: Land of the Dead
item.description: Greg Rucka sends Diana into the underworld in this mythologically dense follow-up to Eyes of the Gorgon, deepening the consequences of her sacrifice and her relationships with gods and mortals alike.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Sacrifice
item.description: Greg Rucka's controversial arc in which Wonder Woman is forced to kill Maxwell Lord to save Superman, a decision with seismic consequences for the DC Universe. One of the most debated and discussed Wonder Woman stories of the modern era.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Stoned
item.description: Phil Jimenez's arc within his run, in which Medusa is resurrected and Diana must face her in a globally televised battle — a precursor to the more famous Rucka treatment and a showcase for Jimenez's mythological ambitions.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Tempest Tossed
item.description: Laurie Halse Anderson and Leila del Duca's YA graphic novel reimagines a teenage Diana as a refugee navigating the modern world, addressing immigration, identity, and activism. Critically praised for its timely themes and accessibility.

item.title: Wonder Woman: The Challenge of Artemis
item.description: William Messner-Loebs and Mike Deodato Jr.'s arc in which Diana is stripped of her title and must fight to reclaim it, introducing a new Wonder Woman in Artemis. Controversial and influential, it directly inspired elements of the animated series.

item.title: Wonder Woman: The Circle
item.description: Gail Simone's defining arc reveals a dark secret from Hippolyta's past — four Amazons sworn to kill the infant Diana — while delivering explosive action and deep character work. Considered the highlight of Simone's celebrated run.

item.title: Wonder Woman: The Hiketeia
item.description: Greg Rucka and J.G. Jones's original graphic novel in which Wonder Woman is bound by ancient Greek law to protect a fugitive hunted by Batman. A taut, mythologically rich examination of Diana's values and their conflict with modern justice.

item.title: Wonder Woman: The Lies
item.description: Greg Rucka's return to Wonder Woman opens with Diana discovering that her memories of Themyscira may be false, launching a psychological and mythological mystery. Part of the celebrated Rebirth-era run that earned widespread critical praise.

item.title: Wonder Woman: The True Amazon
item.description: Jill Thompson's painted original graphic novel reimagines Diana's childhood on Themyscira as a cautionary tale about privilege and entitlement, presenting a flawed, spoiled princess who must earn her heroism. A visually stunning and thematically bold departure.

categories.adaptation_notes: Eisner, Best Graphic Album—New (2017) · Eisner, Best Painter/Multimedia Artist (2017)

item.title: Wonder Woman: The Twelve Labors
item.description: A landmark Bronze Age arc in which Wonder Woman must prove her worthiness to rejoin the Justice League by completing twelve trials observed by each member. Written by multiple creators including Len Wein and Elliot S! Maggin, it marked Diana's feminist reinvention after the controversial de-powered era.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Warkiller
item.description: Gail Simone's arc in which Diana must navigate a war between the Amazons and a tribe of gorilla warriors, blending political allegory with mythic adventure in one of the run's most inventive chapters.

item.title: Wonder Woman: Year One
item.description: Greg Rucka and Nicola Scott's interleaved origin retelling, running alongside The Lies, presents a compassionate and powerful Diana arriving in the world of men for the first time. Widely regarded as one of the finest Wonder Woman origin stories ever told.

item.title: Y: The Last Man

Kingdoms rise, families fracture, and the ocean threatens to swallow everything he holds dear. Through sacrifice, death, and rebirth, Arthur must discover what it means to lead. A crown may make him king, but it is his humanity that makes him Aquaman.

item.name: Captain America: The Promise of the Shield
item.description:
**The Oath. The Shield. The Ideals That Endure.**

Steve Rogers was a frail young man who volunteered to fight tyranny—and woke decades later in a country he barely recognized. From the battlefields of World War II to struggles over political power, civil liberty, and the meaning of patriotism, follow a soldier who learns that serving his country sometimes means standing against those who govern it. Bucky carries the cost of a lost generation. Sam Wilson discovers what it takes to inherit a symbol. Sharon Carter, Peggy Carter, and the people Steve protects remind him that America is more than its institutions. Through betrayal, death, impossible returns, and the passing of the shield, discover why Captain America is ultimately a promise anyone can choose to keep.

item.name: Wonder Woman: The Heart of a Warrior
item.description:
**The Princess. The Warrior. The Ambassador of Peace.**

Born among the Amazons and chosen to champion a world beyond paradise, Diana of Themyscira would become one of Earth's greatest heroes. From the intrigues of Olympus to the battlefields of humanity, follow a princess whose compassion is tested by gods, monsters, and the very people she has sworn to protect. Mothers and daughters clash, sisters rise, and the bonds of love and friendship endure through sacrifice, betrayal, and war. Her strength may rival the gods, but her greatest power has always been the courage to choose mercy when the world demands violence. For above all, Wonder Woman fights not to conquer the world, but to make it worthy of peace.
